A 42-year-old woman visits her primary care physician due to abdominal pain and several months of
watery diarrhea. She also reports persistent thirst and reduced energy levels. Her medical history
includes anxiety and depression, for which she takes fluoxetine. She was recently treated with
amoxicillin-clavulanic acid for a middle ear infection and sinusitis one week ago. Her temperature is
97.8°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 101/54 mmHg, pulse is 73/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen
saturation is 98% on room air. Laboratory findings are as follows: Serum: Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100
mEq/L K+: 2.9 mEq/L HCO3-: 27 mEq/L BUN: 25 mg/dL Glucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL
Ca2+: 10.2 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L A stool culture and ova/parasite examination are negative.
Which of the following is most likely associated with the patient’s diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A)
Impaired zinc absorption (B) Enterotoxin (C) Impaired iron absorption (D) Altered intestinal motility (E)
Increased chloride secretion (F) Increased serotonin production (G) Bacterial overgrowth (H)
Decreased bile acid reabsorption (I) Normal flora destruction (J) Villous atrophy
 A. Impaired zinc absorption
B. Impaired iron absorption
C. Bacterial overgrowth
D. Decreased bile acid reabsorption
E. Altered intestinal motility
F. Increased chloride secretion
G. Villous atrophy
H. Normal flora destruction
I. Enterotoxin
J. Increased serotonin production
